Chapter 6: The Cost of Resistance—Backlash and Burnout.
Have you ever felt that quiet exhaustion... the kind that creeps in when you’re always fighting to be noticed? For so many Black women, pushing back against both racism and sexism means facing resistance from every corner.
The truth is, the world doesn’t always reward those who speak up. In fact, it can punish them.
Imagine a woman who finally finds the courage to call out unfair treatment at work. She’s had enough of being ignored—enough of the jokes and the double standards. When she finally raises her voice, she hopes for support, or at least a little understanding. But instead? She’s met with suspicion. Maybe even outright hostility. Coworkers whisper that she’s “difficult.” Supervisors start questioning her loyalty. Even friends might urge her to just let it go, for the sake of peace.
Most people don’t realize just how isolating it feels to stand alone. And the cost? It’s not just about your job. It goes so much deeper. That constant stress of always being on guard, the fear of retaliation, and the weight of being misunderstood—it can really wear you down. Some days, it just feels easier to stay silent. To swallow the hurt and keep moving.
But silence isn’t free, either. Over time, the pressure builds up. Maybe you start snapping at the people you love, tossing and turning at night, or finding that things you used to love just don’t bring you joy anymore. The world keeps telling you to be strong—but nobody ever asks what it actually costs to carry that strength.
Still, there are these powerful moments of connection that make the struggle a little more bearable. Maybe a coworker quietly offers you some support. Or a friend listens—really listens—without judgment. Or a mentor shares her own story of survival. Little acts of solidarity that remind you you’re not alone. That your pain is real. And that your resistance truly matters.
So here’s the key takeaway: The fight for justice isn’t just about changing the world outside. It’s also about caring for yourself—and for each other—along the way. Rest, laughter, and community? They’re not luxuries. They’re essentials for survival.
